articles.title: Proofpoint CEO Sumit Dhawan- ‘Very Excited’ for $6.3 Billion Varonis Acquisition
articles.summary:
How is artificial intelligence reshaping cybersecurity, and why is data security becoming one of the most important challenges facing enterprises?

In this NYSE Live interview, Sumit Dhawan, CEO of Proofpoint, discusses the company's planned $6.3 billion acquisition of Varonis, the growing importance of data security in the AI era, and how the combined company aims to address evolving cybersecurity threats.

JD Durkin spoke with Dhawan about artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, enterprise data protection, AI-related security risks, platform consolidation, and the future of cybersecurity strategy.

A major theme throughout the conversation is the growing convergence of artificial intelligence and cybersecurity. As organizations accelerate AI adoption, protecting sensitive enterprise data has become a top priority for executive teams, boards of directors, and security leaders.

The interview also explores the rationale behind Proofpoint's acquisition of Varonis. According to Dhawan, the transaction is designed to create a more comprehensive platform for protecting enterprise data as organizations navigate increasingly complex cybersecurity environments.

Another key topic is the emergence of data as the next frontier of cybersecurity. Traditional security architectures were not necessarily built to address the challenges posed by modern AI systems that depend on vast volumes of organizational data.

The conversation further examines how AI is changing the threat landscape. Advanced AI systems can be leveraged by attackers to launch sophisticated social engineering campaigns, create highly personalized phishing attacks, and automate malicious activity at unprecedented scale.

A significant focus of the discussion is the importance of securing data throughout its lifecycle. Organizations must not only protect information where it is stored but also ensure it remains secure as employees, applications, and AI systems interact with it.

The interview also highlights concerns around AI agents and autonomous systems. As enterprises deploy increasingly capable AI technologies, managing access controls, permissions, and data governance becomes even more critical.

Another major theme is platform consolidation within cybersecurity. Many security leaders are seeking fewer, more integrated technology providers as they work to reduce complexity and improve visibility across their environments.

The discussion also explores how Proofpoint and Varonis bring complementary capabilities to the market. Varonis specializes in protecting data at rest, while Proofpoint focuses on safeguarding data as it moves through human interactions, communications, and enterprise workflows.

Additionally, Dhawan explains how effective data security can accelerate AI adoption. Organizations that are confident in their ability to secure and govern information may be better positioned to deploy advanced AI solutions at scale.
The interview further examines strategic priorities among enterprise technology leaders. Data governance, cybersecurity resilience, and AI readiness continue moving higher on executive agendas as organizations assess both opportunities and risks.

Another key topic is the future structure of the cybersecurity industry. Dhawan believes organizations increasingly prefer strategic platform providers capable of delivering broad protection rather than relying on large collections of disconnected security tools.

The conversation also highlights Proofpoint's ambition to become a leading provider of data and AI security solutions as organizations continue modernizing their security architectures.

Looking ahead, Dhawan expects demand for integrated data security platforms to continue growing as enterprises invest 
in artificial intelligence, automation, and next-generation digital transformation initiatives.

Throughout the discussion, Dhawan shares insights on artificial intelligence, enterprise security, cybersecurity platforms, data governance, risk management, AI adoption, cyber threats, digital transformation, platform consolidation, and data protection.
